subject: Cross-region safeguard proposal and pin schedule
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@optih.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@optih.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency commitments & transient failover question

Jordan / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OptiHealth is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move deeper I'd like to close a couple of open items on residency guarantees and what happens during transient cross-region processing. Two concrete asks from our DPO and procurement: 

1) Can Redwood provide a binding schedule for region pinning (EU/APAC/US) by environment (prod, staging, analytics) and an SLA for temporary cross-hop that includes max duration and notification expectations?
2) For any transient cross-region processing, what telemetry will you provide (per-request region tag, egress timestamps, and KMS key rotation notes)? We need this to satisfy our internal audit and to map to our DPA annex.

I attached a simple SOW matrix that shows what we expect by environment — happy to walk through.

Marta
Data Protection Officer
OptiHealth Inc
[Attachment: OptiHealth_SOW_pin_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@optih.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency commitments & transient failover question

Marta — thanks for the clear asks and the matrix. High level answers up front: yes, we can provide a per-environment pin schedule and an operational SLA for controlled transient cross-hop; and yes, we can surface per-request region tags, egress timestamps, and KMS key metadata in the audit logs.

That said, there are two flavors of temporary processing we typically discuss:
- Graceful failover (planned maintenance / region-wide maintenance windows) — usually we provide a 72-hour notice window and a max 48h transient hop for production traffic unless an emergency forces a longer window.
- Capacity-driven short hops (unplanned) — these are limited to short bursts (minutes to a few hours) and we can bind them with additional telemetry + a documented rollback policy.

To be concrete, I've attached our transient hop runbook (ops-level) and propose a short MAP (mutual action plan):
- Week 1: Redwood to provide a per-environment pin schedule draft
- Week 2: Ops call to walk the telemetry payload and log format (we'll send sample JSON)
- Week 3: Sign DPA annex with the annexed pin matrix and notification SLA

Can Laura (legal/partner ops) and Marissa (customer success) join an ops walkthrough on Wed or Thu?

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_transient_hop_runbook_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@optih.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency commitments & transient failover question

Marta — looping in ops/legal for the technical telemetry and subprocessors. Quick clarifications from our side to make the annex precise: 

- "Pin schedule" — we mean a binding statement in the DPA addendum that lists which regions will process customer content for each environment and the maximum allowed transient hop duration and trigger conditions.
- "Notification SLA" — we propose 24h notice for planned maintenance and real-time alerting for unplanned short hops (via the console + webhook).
- "Subprocessors" — we'll provide a snapshot roster for the next 90 days and include a clause for 14-day notice before activating a new infra subprocessor in the pinned region.

Operational ask: Connor, can you prepare a sample audit log snippet that includes: request_id, region_in, region_out (if different), egress_ts, model_id, and kms_key_alias? We will share that during the walkthrough.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Laura / Jordan — that all sounds reasonable. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and our infra team: 

- Procurement insists on a concrete maximum not a range (e.g., "max transient hop 72 hours for planned, 6 hours for unplanned bursts") and a financial credit if exceeded. Can Redwood commit to a credit policy for SLA breach in the annex?
- Our infra team wants assurance that caching (KV/prefix caching) will not cause persistent replication outside the pinned region beyond the declared window.

We're available for the ops walkthrough on Thu 5/6 at 08:00 PT if that works for Redwood (we'll bring a security engineer).

Marta

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency commitments & transient failover question

Thanks all for the call earlier — notes and next steps below. Forwarding the sample audit log snippet and the TTL behavior for cache eviction as discussed.

Call highlights:
- Pin schedule: Prod EU / APAC / US pinned — staging pinned to EU/US only — analytics may be set to US by default but can be limited per contract.
- Max durations: Planned maintenance transient hop capped at 72 hours (annexed SLA). Unplanned short hops capped at 6 hours for production (we will set a rolling threshold at 6 hours and trigger immediate remediation).
- Credits: Redwood proposes a tiered credit: 10% monthly credit for single incident exceeding the cap; 25% if >2 incidents in rolling 30 days. Legal is drafting annex language for this.
- Cache behavior: KV/prefix cache entries will be stamped with region_of_origin metadata and a configurable TTL; any entry that would persist outside pinned region beyond the TTL will be auto-evicted or scrubbed. We will include an ops API to force eviction during audit.
- Subprocessors: current roster for APAC will be attached to the HubSpot deal; new infra subprocessors will follow 14-day notice + opt-out carveout for enterprise.

Attachments from call: runbook excerpt, sample_audit_log.json, proposed_SLA_paragraphs.docx

Next steps:
1) Laura to circulate DPA annex draft with the pin matrix and credit table (EOD Fri).
2) Jordan / Marissa to finalize MAP and confirm rollout date.
3) Connor to upload sample audit logs + cache eviction API spec to the shared Drive link.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
